final_proof:
Let X be the set of points, with |X| = v, and let 𝓑 be the collection of blocks, with |𝓑| = b. Thus every block contains exactly k points, and every pair of distinct points is contained in exactly λ blocks. As usual for an incomplete BIBD, 1 < k < v and λ > 0.

For a point x in X, let r_x denote the number of blocks containing x. Count the pairs (y,B) such that y is in X minus {x}, B is in 𝓑, and x,y are both in B. On the one hand, each of the r_x blocks containing x supplies k − 1 choices for y, so the number of such pairs is r_x(k − 1). On the other hand, there are v − 1 choices for y, and the pair {x,y} lies in exactly λ blocks, so the number is λ(v − 1). Hence

r_x(k − 1) = λ(v − 1).

It follows that r_x is independent of x; denote this common value by r. Moreover,

r − λ = λ((v − 1)/(k − 1) − 1) = λ(v − k)/(k − 1) > 0.

Now let N be the v by b incidence matrix of the design: its (x,B)-entry is 1 if x is in B, and 0 otherwise. The diagonal entry (NNᵀ)_(x,x) equals the number of blocks containing x, namely r, while for distinct points x,y, the entry (NNᵀ)_(x,y) equals the number of blocks containing both, namely λ. Consequently,

NNᵀ = (r − λ)I_v + λJ_v,

where I_v is the identity matrix and J_v is the all-ones matrix. For every nonzero vector z = (z_x)_(x in X) in R^v,

zᵀNNᵀz = (r − λ) Σ_(x in X) z_x² + λ(Σ_(x in X) z_x)² > 0,

because r − λ > 0. Thus NNᵀ is positive definite and therefore has rank v. Since the image of NNᵀ is contained in the image of N,

v = rank(NNᵀ) ≤ rank(N) ≤ b.

Therefore b ≥ v, as required.
